.order-menu-choice and .order-menu-inspect both declare min-height: var(--touch-target), and .order-menu is an auto-fit grid with minmax(16rem, 1fr) — 16rem is 256px, comfortably inside 375. So the barrier is unlikely to report on arrival, but I had not yet finished checking .order-basket-controls, .order-send and the two quantity inputs when I hit the tool limit.

Slice 64 is authored but not packaged — I hit the tool limit before I could build the archive
I have to be plain about this rather than hand you something half-finished. The working tree in my sandbox holds the slice, but I ran out of tool calls before tar-ing it, and that sandbox does not survive this turn. Nothing is deliverable from this response. The next session re-authors from dump.txt and packages in one go.

What is worth having now is the finding, because you can verify it in about ten seconds and it is real.

F-118 — the guest's basket has a form control that no rule in your stylesheet reaches
TableOrderSurface.razor renders the staged line's quantity box like this:

razor
<label class="order-basket-quantity">
    <span>Quantity</span>
    <input type="number" inputmode="numeric" ... />
</label>
That <label> is not a .form-field and not a .manage-inline-form — the only two selector lists in app.css that carry the nine control declarations. Grep app.css for every rule matching an input and you get: .form-field input (535), .manage-inline-form input (1665), the checkbox rules, and this:

css
.order-picker-quantity input,
.order-basket-quantity input {
    max-width: 8rem;
}
max-width is the only rule in the whole stylesheet that touches it. So that control has neither half of §11.12:

No min-height: var(--touch-target) → roughly 21px tall, against a 44px floor.
No font: inherit / font-size: max(1rem, 1em) → the UA default, about 13.3px, against a 16px floor.
And the 16px floor is not a preference. §11.12 says it in as many words: iOS Safari zooms the whole viewport on a focused control under 16px and does not zoom back. This is on the guest's basket — the one surface R§1 names when it says guests order from their own phones.

Why it survived. The two quantity boxes are named side by side in that max-width rule, which reads as a pair treated alike, while the declarations deciding whether they are alike sit two hundred lines away. .order-picker-quantity is inside a .form-field and inherited the rule; .order-basket-quantity inherited nothing. It is F-66's shape a second time — that was four administration detail surfaces declaring form controls inline with no touch-target height at all.

Why nothing could catch it. HandheldLayoutContractTests asserts the declaration exists in app.css and cannot know which element a page renders. The 375px barrier could have seen it and is scoped to §11.4. Whether a declared rule reaches a rendered element is a third question sitting between your two levels, and only a computed style read off a real element answers it.

Where the slice stands
Confirmed at session start: tree at 3e90d18, Slice 63, v1.48, floor 37, F-117, 381 of 383 files SHA-256 verified (export.sh and LICENSE are the two that never verify). Your run gives 1302 passed, 0 failed — so Slices 62 and 63 are both confirmed at once, and 1302 is now an observation rather than a prediction for the first time in four slices.

The slice I wrote closes the plan's line 1049 — "Nothing in this repository measures §11.1 at 375px" — as Stage 1d, and it is what found F-118.

File	State
wwwroot/app.css	.order-basket-quantity input joins the .form-field selector list (repair is a selector, never a third copy of the declarations)
Harness/HandheldReach.cs	rewritten: HandheldSurface as a value, Administration and GuestOrder, MeasureHereAsync for interactive surfaces, per-selector census, required/optional selectors, a font-floor verdict
Harness/TableJourneys.cs	SeatGuestAsync gains handheld = false — default, so no existing caller moves
MenuReactionScenarios.cs	guest seated at 375×667; steps (k)(l)(m) stage a line, reopen the 86'd dish's panel, and measure
TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION.md	v1.49 — §11.12's third-question paragraph, §16.3 scenario 21, §16.4's barrier description, F-118 and Stage 1d in Appendix A
DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md, MENU_AND_HANDHELD_PLAN.md, BUILD_PROGRESS.md, _CHANGES.md	not yet written
Predicted count stays 1302 — no test class is added and no [Fact] moves; §16.3 stays at 21. MinimumCountedClasses stays 37.

What is worth having now is the finding, because you can verify it in about ten seconds and it is real.

F-118 — the guest's basket has a form control that no rule in your stylesheet reaches
TableOrderSurface.razor renders the staged line's quantity box like this:

razor
<label class="order-basket-quantity">
    <span>Quantity</span>
    <input type="number" inputmode="numeric" ... />
</label>
That <label> is not a .form-field and not a .manage-inline-form — the only two selector lists in app.css that carry the nine control declarations. Grep app.css for every rule matching an input and you get: .form-field input (535), .manage-inline-form input (1665), the checkbox rules, and this:

css
.order-picker-quantity input,
.order-basket-quantity input {
    max-width: 8rem;
}
max-width is the only rule in the whole stylesheet that touches it. So that control has neither half of §11.12:

No min-height: var(--touch-target) → roughly 21px tall, against a 44px floor.
No font: inherit / font-size: max(1rem, 1em) → the UA default, about 13.3px, against a 16px floor.
And the 16px floor is not a preference. §11.12 says it in as many words: iOS Safari zooms the whole viewport on a focused control under 16px and does not zoom back. This is on the guest's basket — the one surface R§1 names when it says guests order from their own phones.

Why it survived. The two quantity boxes are named side by side in that max-width rule, which reads as a pair treated alike, while the declarations deciding whether they are alike sit two hundred lines away. .order-picker-quantity is inside a .form-field and inherited the rule; .order-basket-quantity inherited nothing. It is F-66's shape a second time — that was four administration detail surfaces declaring form controls inline with no touch-target height at all.

Why nothing could catch it. HandheldLayoutContractTests asserts the declaration exists in app.css and cannot know which element a page renders. The 375px barrier could have seen it and is scoped to §11.4. Whether a declared rule reaches a rendered element is a third question sitting between your two levels, and only a computed style read off a real element answers it.
